newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI relaxes norms for expatriate investments.
newsitem.headline: India RBI relaxes norms for expatriate investments.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday announced relaxations in the norms for investments in unlisted Indian firms by expatriate Indians and overseas corporate bodies.
The relaxations in the norms announced by the RBI are:
*Further liberalisation in the present scheme for 100 percent investments in loss-making units by expatriate Indians.

*General permission would be granted for interest-free non-repatriable loans from expatriate relatives for personal purposes and for business activities. Interest-free repatriable loans up to $250,000 would be cleared by the RBI automatically. Other cases would continue to be cleared by the RBI on a case by case basis.
*RBI will permit the transfer of funds from one non-resident (external) (NRE) account to the NRE account of another person.
*Expatriate Indians/overseas corporate bodies shall be permitted to establish schools and colleges on the same terms and conditions as a resident individual/corporate body.
*The existing 40 percent scheme will be abolished and investment by expatriate Indians/overseas corporate bodies will be allowed in unlisted companies up to 51 percent on a repatriation basis.
*Participation by expatriate Indians in venture capital activity will be permitted on the same terms and conditions as foreign investment in this area.
*Housing finance companies will be permitted to grant loans to expatriate Indians for acquisition/improvement to the existing houses on the same terms and conditions as applicable to residents.
The RBI said detailed instructions would be issued shortly.
